meta.question: Is the 23% cascade-ion deficit in the primary track or the secondary cascade, and is it a real physics shortfall or a counting convention?
meta.method: Analysed the full 6.76 GB Geant4 dnaphysics ntuple (dna.root, 115.5M steps, 4096 events at 10 keV) with uproot: counted e-_G4DNAIonisation steps (flagProcess==13) split by trackID==1 (primary) vs >1 (secondary). Compared to our ionisation-EVENT counts read natively (dbg[0]=primary, secStats[4]=secondary).

summary.headline: PRIMARY track ionisations match Geant4 EXACTLY (195.4 vs 195.6, 1.00x) — the primary track structure is validated bit-on. The ENTIRE cascade deficit is the SECONDARY cascade: 216.9 vs 313.6 (0.69x, 31% low). Our secondary electrons under-multiply (ionise less on the way down than Geant4).
summary.conclusion: Resolves the cascade deficit: it is NOT the primary physics (perfect match), NOT a counting convention (same e-_G4DNAIonisation definition, primary matches), and NOT energy misallocation (E19). It is specifically the secondary-electron cascade under-ionising by 31%. The next investigation is the low-energy (~10-100 eV) secondary ionisation — cross section magnitude or the 7.4 eV tracking cutoff truncating the cascade. This is now a single, sharply-defined, WGSL-side-fixable target.
